children: Shares of the newly merged Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery have shaved an additional 8% during its second day of trading as concerns over a sizable debt load, the logistics of integrating two major movie studios, and ambitious production targets have investors staying on the sidelines.
was created on October 6 with a centuries-old content library, 4 streaming channels, sports rights to the NFL, MLB, and NASCAR, and a news division with few rivals.
The company also comes with more than $80B in debt, a recent credit downgrade, and an unproven financial history in an environment of intense competition and a changing AI-fueled landscape.

Co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz tried to soothe investors’ concerns over the debt load with a multi-year plan that includes mid-single-digit revenue growth through 2030, at least $6B in run-rate synergies within three years, and free cash flow conversion of ~50%, all of which will help the company achieve net leverage of 3.75x in 2028 and 3x in 2029.

However, shareholder value will ultimately depend on whether management can grow streaming profits faster than the decline in the legacy TV business, says UBS analyst John Hodulik, an endeavor that seems even more daunting when you consider that legacy TV currently accounts for at least two-thirds of Skydance’s
“We expect shares to be volatile given the pending issuance of stock warrants and low stock float,” Hodulik adds.
The company is set to distribute ~470M warrants on October 13, giving holders of Class B Paramount Skydance shares the option to purchase Class B shares of Skydance

common stock for $12 per share within a 10-year period. This will give PSKY holders the opportunity to buy shares in the new company on similar terms to investors that participated in the $47B equity syndicate.
Barron’s estimates that the warrants could trade for around $3 each on the open market. While the warrants currently have no intrinsic value because their $12 exercise price is above Skydance’s

current share price, they still carry value based on the potential for the stock to rise above $12 over the next 10 years. The warrants could also provide a potential catalyst for the shares if investors become more optimistic about Skydance’s long-term prospects.

title: Skydance shares extend decline as debt, streaming challenges weigh
